name: Truck-Launched Deep-Strike FPV Swarm
representative_system: Composite representation of Ukraine's 'Operation Spiderweb' method (June 1, 2025) — FPV drones smuggled by commercial truck and launched from inside Russian territory

cost.display: Individual FPV airframes cost roughly the same as any other FPV drone (low thousands of dollars each); the operation's value is asymmetric — an estimated $7B in damage to a fleet of strategic bombers from a low-cost drone/logistics effort

key_facts.label: Confirmed reach
key_facts.value: 4,300 km from Ukraine (Belaya airbase, Irkutsk region)

key_facts.label: Method
key_facts.value: FPV drones hidden in modified trucks, launched via remote-opened roof panels

short_role: Not a single vehicle — a method: FPV drones smuggled deep into enemy territory by truck, then launched within a few kilometers of the target itself.
characteristics: Airframes are ordinary short-range FPV drones, not long-range cruise missiles — the 'range' comes from covert ground transport, not flight endurance
Trucks with remotely-opened roof panels released drones roughly within line of sight of the target airbases
Reportedly planned and staged over an extended period, smuggling components in disguised as ordinary cargo
Struck strategic bomber types (Tu-95, Tu-22M3, Tu-160) and an A-50 airborne early-warning aircraft
employment_notes: This entry's distance on the map (~4,300 km) represents the operation's confirmed reach, not a drone physically flying that far — the FPV airframes themselves only had to cover the last few kilometers from a parked truck to the target. The distance is achieved by defeating border and internal security over months, not by any flight characteristic of the drone. Deliberately minimal live operator control was used near the target for exactly the reason doctrine calls out about deconfliction and detection risk this deep in denied territory.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional deep-strike doctrine assumed reach came from a missile's range or an aircraft's radius of action, and that a target 4,300 km from the front was accordingly safe. Smuggling ordinary short-range FPV drones to within line of sight of the target collapses that assumption entirely — the front line and national borders stop being a meaningful protective distance at all once the delivery method is a truck rather than a missile, which is as significant a shift as the minutes-scale kill chain described elsewhere in this doctrine set.

notable_events.title: Operation Spiderweb
notable_events.description: 117 FPV drones, smuggled into Russia by truck over an extended covert operation, launched simultaneously against 5 strategic bomber airbases up to 4,300 km from Ukraine (including Belaya in Irkutsk region, Siberia). Reportedly struck 41 aircraft including Tu-95, Tu-22M3 and Tu-160 strategic bombers and an A-50 airborne early-warning aircraft — estimated at billions of dollars in damage to Russia's strategic bomber fleet.
